topic: New Gas Consortium (Soyo) non-associated gas feed and ownership restructuring
wiki_text: In November 2025 Angola achieved first production from the New Gas Consortium (NGC) — the country's first non-associated gas development — and inaugurated a ~US$4 billion onshore gas treatment plant at Soyo, adjacent to Angola LNG. The NGC (operated by Azule Energy alongside Cabinda Gulf Oil Company, Sonangol E&P and TotalEnergies) draws gas from the offshore Quiluma and Maboqueiro fields, with initial throughput around 400 MMscf/d and a planned ramp toward end-2026. Gas from the Soyo plant feeds the Angola LNG facility, securing dedicated (non-associated) feedstock for LNG exports and domestic supply. Separately, Angola LNG's ownership was restructured when BP and Eni combined their Angolan interests into the 50:50 JV Azule Energy (since 2022), which now holds their combined ~27.2% participation; current shareholders are Chevron, Azule Energy, Sonangol and TotalEnergies.
